pages.name: Bolt Warden
pages.text: A clockwork crew for your defences. It has no weapon of its own: its whole job is to man an $(l)Emplacement$() and work the crossbow on it.$(br2)$(o)Work in progress: placeholder looks, and it may still change.$()

pages.title: Winding It Up
pages.text: Stand three $(l)stripped logs$() in a row on top of a fourth, like a T. Use a $(l)Mechanical Trigger$() on the middle log of the top row and the logs become a Bolt Warden.$(br2)The trigger is its heart: it drops again if the warden is destroyed.
The Emplacement faces the way you look when you place it. That facing is the middle of its firing cone, 45° either side.

pages.title: Arming a Post
pages.text: Right-click the emplacement with a $(l)crossbow$() to mount it and with a $(l)quiver$() to fit its ammunition. Arrows top the quiver up. Empty-handed, you take back the quiver, or the crossbow while sneaking.$(br2)A comparator reads how full the quiver is, and a redstone signal holds its fire.

pages.title: On Watch
pages.text: A warden keeps within 16 blocks of where it was built, and crews any post in that area. When a hostile mob enters a loaded post's cone, it runs to that post, reloads at the crossbow's own speed and fires.$(br2)Range is 16 blocks, 32 with a $(l)Scope$(). A $(l)Magazine$() fires in bursts.

pages.title: Rules of Engagement
pages.text: Wardens only ever shoot hostile mobs, and hold fire while anyone else stands in the line. Every shot wears the crossbow down, the bolts can be picked back up, and kills give no archery experience: the warden pulled the trigger, not you.
